title: Late check-out on a same-day turnover
summary: Synthetic facts from a PMS and a housekeeping system for one property. A late check-out is granted in a unit already assigned to an arrival the same day. Replay events.jsonl in file order through an implementation and compare its dispositions, readiness and situations with expected.json. The situations are non-normative; the dispositions follow the HOS Events 0.1 processing rules.
covers: A unit held by another guest in house is not ready
Late check-out overlapping a same-day arrival
Occupancy observed by a non-authoritative producer
Latest plan wins: an older stay plan replayed late is superseded
Delivery order differs from occurrence order

deliveries.note: Stay stay_3088 was booked on 30 June, from 18 August at 16:00 to 21 August at the standard 11:00 check-out.
The PMS assigned unit 1207 to stay_3088 on 18 August.
The guest of stay_3088 checked in on 18 August at 17:10.
The PMS created reservation res_3140 on 3 August for an arrival on 21 August.
Stay stay_3140 is expected on 21 August at the standard 16:00 check-in.

At 07:30 on 21 August the PMS assigns unit 1207 to the arriving stay: a same-day turnover. The guest of stay_3088 still holds the unit, so it is not ready. That guest is due to leave at 11:00, before the arrival, so there is no situation.

At 09:15 a front-desk agent grants stay_3088 a late check-out at 17:00. The PMS publishes the stay's new planned times. The guest in house is now due to leave after the 16:00 check-in: the reference projection raises arrival.room_readiness_at_risk, naming the stay that holds the unit.

At 12:40 a room attendant finds unit 1207 empty and reports it vacant. The housekeeping manifest declares occupancy non-authoritative: the guest may only be out, luggage still in the room. Only the PMS says who holds the unit.
A PMS replay delivers the stay's plan from 20 August, with the 11:00 check-out. Applied, it would make the risk seem resolved. It is older than the late check-out, so it is superseded.

The housekeeping system reports unit 1207 dirty after the departure at 13:55, before the PMS check-out reaches HOS. It changes the housekeeping status only: the PMS still says the guest holds the unit, so the risk remains.

The PMS check-out, which occurred at 13:50, arrives late. The unit is vacated before the arrival: the risk is resolved as unit_vacated. The unit is dirty, but the guest is expected at 16:00, not earlier.
The housekeeping system opens a high-priority cleaning task, due at check-in. Its causal link points to the dirty status.
The cleaning is done at 15:05. At this property only an inspection releases a unit, so it is still dirty.
Unit 1207 is inspected at 15:20. The arriving stay is ready.
The guest of stay_3140 checks in at 16:10.
